title: Contract Foundational Skills
delivery: Virtual instructor-led (VILT), full time. A classroom version, CON 1100, also counts.
prereq_text: None. You must finish it before CON 1200V and CON 1400V.
short_about: First course: the acquisition process, researching the regulations, and professional skills.
about: Your first course. It covers the basics every contracting professional needs: an overview of the acquisition process, how to find and research the regulations (FAR, DFARS and agency supplements), and the soft and professional skills you will use for your whole career.
learn: How the federal acquisition process fits together, from requirement to closeout
How the FAR, DFARS and AFARS are organized, and how to research them
Contracting authority and the roles on the acquisition team
Professional skills: communication, critical thinking and working with customers
before: About 2.5 hours of pre-work. Finish it before day one.
In this guide, read the Guiding Principles lessons, especially The rulebook and Who can bind the Government.
Test your camera, microphone and the class software on the computer you will use.
pass: Treat the course as full-time duty: no email, no side tasks.
Practice finding things in the FAR; looking things up quickly is the skill you will use most.
Ask questions and use the instructors' office hours.
notes: While the FAR Overhaul (RFO) rules are going through rulemaking, CON 1100 runs 4 full days; it returns to 8 days afterward.
Class details arrive in the welcome letter about 25 days before class.

title: Contract Pre-award
delivery: Virtual instructor-led (VILT), full time, with a self-paced part
short_about: Pre-award: shaping the requirement, strategy, acquisition plan and solicitation.
about: Everything that happens before offers arrive: the business relationship between Government and industry, defining and shaping the customer's requirement, building a contract strategy and acquisition plan, and writing and releasing the solicitation. A short online module, CON 1210 (Contract Pre-Award: Industry Perspective), is built into the class time.
learn: Working with the customer to define the requirement (PWS, SOW or SOO)
Market research and acquisition planning
Choosing a contract type and a contracting method
Required sources and small business programs
Building, releasing and amending a solicitation
before: Read the Pre-Award lessons in this guide.
Learn the FAR part titles for Parts 5 through 19; you will use them all week.
Ask your office for a sample PWS and a sample solicitation to look at.
pass: Expect group work on a realistic requirement; take an active role.
Keep a one-page cheat sheet of thresholds and posting times as you go.
Connect each exercise back to the FAR part it comes from.
notes: The course needs your full attention for all nine days.

title: Contract Award
prereq_text: CON 1200V, plus FAC 069, FAC 082 and FAC 085 before class, and CON 0074 and CON 0470 before or during class
short_about: Award: price or cost analysis, negotiation, source selection and protests.
about: How offers become a contract: conducting price or cost analysis, planning and conducting negotiations, selecting the source, and understanding protests.
learn: Price analysis and cost analysis, and when each applies
Planning negotiations and writing negotiation objectives
Evaluating offers and supporting a source selection decision
Debriefings and protests
before: Finish the five online modules first: FAC 069, FAC 082, FAC 085, CON 0074 and CON 0470. Keep every completion certificate: the instructor needs CON 0074 and CON 0470 to give you credit (CON 0070 or CON 0072 can stand in for CON 0074).
Watch the optional negotiation simulation linked from the course page.
Read the Award lessons in this guide and practice the price analysis questions.
pass: Give the course 100% of your time; the instructors expect it.
Show your math in pricing exercises; the method matters as much as the answer.
Read FAR Part 15 alongside the course; the exam leans on it.
notes: CON 7300V Price Analysis comes after this course.

title: Price Analysis
delivery: VILT: 3 self-paced days with office hours, then 4 instructor-led days
short_about: Price Analysis: required since 1 October 2026, after CON 1300V.
about: Required for the DoW Contracting Professional certification since 1 October 2026. Hands-on price analysis: applying the techniques in FAR 15.404-1 (comparing proposed prices, prior prices, parametric estimates and more), using market research and technical analysis, spotting unbalanced pricing, and documenting a fair and reasonable price. It ends with a graded capstone simulation.
learn: Choosing the right proposal analysis technique for the situation
Using market research and the customer's requirement in your analysis
Every price analysis technique in FAR 15.404-1, as supplemented by the DFARS and PGI
Working with technical evaluators
Evaluating unit prices and spotting unbalanced pricing
Documenting a fair and reasonable price
before: Get comfortable with Excel. If you are not, take an Excel course first (the catalog suggests HOS 0013, Excel Skills for Business Intermediate I).
Review the price analysis lesson and the 1300V pricing exercises.
pass: Day 1 starts with a mandatory one-hour session in the morning. Days 2 and 3 are self-paced with office hours each afternoon: use them.
Days 4 to 7 are mandatory instructor-led sessions. Day 6 introduces the graded simulation; day 7 finishes it.
Save your workbook calculations; you will reuse them on the job.
notes: Registration priority goes to people who are working on their certification.
If you started your certification before 1 October 2026, your component decides whether you must take it; DoW expects you to.

title: Contract Post-Award
prereq_text: CON 1100 or CON 1100V (you do not need 1200V or 1300V first)
short_about: Post-award: administration, quality, payments, changes, disputes, terminations and closeout.
about: Running a contract after award, in four units that follow the post-award life cycle: roles and communication with the contractor; monitoring performance and quality; payments, files and funds; changes, subcontracts, disputes, terminations and closeout. Updated for the FAR Overhaul for classes starting on or after 11 May 2026.
learn: Roles, responsibilities and communication between the Government and the contractor
Monitoring performance with quality assurance and surveillance
Administering payments, contract files and funds
Processing changes, managing subcontracts and small business subcontracting plans
Resolving disputes and terminations
Closing out a contract
before: Read the Post-Award lessons in this guide.
Ask your office to show you a real modification and a closeout checklist.
pass: Scenario exercises mirror real problems; think about what you would do in your own office.
Know which changes the contracting officer can make alone and which need the contractor's agreement.
notes: Because it only needs CON 1100, you can take it any time after CON 1100 to fill a gap in your schedule.

title: Price Analysis (online module)
about: A short online course on price analysis basics. Finish it before CON 1300V and keep the certificate.
learn: What price analysis is and why it comes first
Common ways to compare prices

title: B2B: Conduct Pre-award and Post-award Debriefings
about: How to tell offerors why they were excluded or did not win, before and after award. Finish it before CON 1300V.
learn: When an offeror is entitled to a debriefing
What a debriefing must and must not include

title: B2B: Price Reasonableness for Simplified Acquisitions
about: How to decide a price is fair and reasonable on a simplified buy, where most new specialists start. Finish it before CON 1300V.
learn: Using competitive quotes, prior prices, catalogs and market research
Documenting your decision

title: Source Selection (online module)
prereq_text: Before or during CON 1300V. CON 0070 or CON 0072 can stand in for it.
about: The source selection process from evaluation factors to the decision. CON 1300V needs your completion certificate.

title: Contract Negotiation Techniques (online module)
about: Negotiation basics: planning, positions, tactics and documenting the result. CON 1300V needs your completion certificate.

title: Online Contracting Certification Exam Prep
delivery: Online, self-paced, available as soon as you register
short_about: Online exam prep with practice quizzes and a practice exam.
about: Self-paced lessons, practice quizzes and a practice exam built to get you ready for CON 3990V. DoW strongly encourages it before your first attempt, and it is the prerequisite for CON 3900V.
pass: Take its practice exam under real conditions: closed book, timed.
Use this guide's exam simulator and flashcards alongside it.

title: Contracting Certification Exam Prep Course
short_about: Instructor-led exam prep; required before a retest after a failed first attempt.
about: Instructor-led exam prep: test-taking strategies, how the exam is built, and learner-led exercises. If you fail your first attempt, DoW requires it before you test again. People retesting get priority, so others may be wait-listed.

title: Contracting Certification Exam
delivery: Proctored by Pearson VUE at a test center or online (OnVUE)
prereq_text: Coded in the contracting functional area and your supervisor's approval. CON 3910 or CON 3900V recommended first.
short_about: The exam: 150 questions, 3 hours, closed book, 70% to pass.
about: The closed-book exam that shows you have the initial readiness to do contracting work: 150 multiple-choice questions, 3 hours, 70% to pass. Questions cover the Contracting Common Technical Competencies, and the right answers come from the RFO-updated FAR and DFARS. Passing it does not replace any course.
pass: Weight your study like the exam: Guiding Principles 42, Award 40, Post-Award 38, Pre-Award 30.
Read FAR Part 15 thoroughly.
Take it at a test center if you can.

title: DoW Governmentwide Commercial Purchase Card Overview
about: How the purchase card (GPC) works in DoW: who may use it, the micro-purchase rules, and the controls that keep cardholders out of trouble. Useful in any office that supports cardholders.

title: Market Research
about: A deeper look at market research: sources, techniques and how the results shape the acquisition strategy.

title: Art & Science of Contracting
about: A short course on how contracting decisions get made in practice. Recommended by WarU for purchasing and small business work.

title: Services Acquisition
about: Buying services the right way: performance-based requirements, surveillance and avoiding personal services. Recommended for contingency contracting.

title: Contingency Contracting Simulation: Barda Bridge
about: A contingency contracting simulation. WarU recommends it for the contingency contracting assignment, which is most 51C work.

title: Critical Concepts in Operational Contract Support
about: How contracting supports operations: planning, contractor management and the people involved. Good background for deploying 51Cs.
